scope: Bounded C3GN map: alternative complement pathway dysregulation, acquired convertase stabilization, complement-regulatory variants and glomerular complement deposition. Dense deposit disease is excluded as a phenotype; mixed C3 glomerulopathy studies are labelled and cannot establish C3GN-specific effects. Infection-related and immune-complex glomerulonephritis are excluded.

paragraphs.text: C3 glomerulonephritis comprises heterogeneous complement-associated kidney injury rather than a single universal circuit. C3GN biopsies and clinical series link alternative-pathway abnormalities with glomerular complement deposits, hematuria and proteinuria. Patient-IgG experiments show that nephritic factors can stabilize C3 convertase, but the classic assay cohort was predominantly dense deposit disease, and terminal-pathway activity varied between samples. Familial evidence identifies a different branch: a CFHR5 duplication cosegregated with C3GN and produced a protein with altered surface-complement binding; its increased cofactor activity argues against a simple loss of all function. CFHR3-1 rearrangements provide another familial association. These mechanisms remain incomplete: more than half of the C3GN subgroup in a modern comprehensively characterized cohort had no identifiable driver. Local glomerular dysregulation is a proposed explanation, not a demonstrated mechanism for that group.

Clinical course and treatment response also vary. Stable function in a small native-kidney C3GN series does not negate progression seen in the expanded CFHR5 founder cohort. In mixed-population randomized trials, iptacopan reduced proteinuria versus placebo by 35.1% at six months and pegcetacoplan by 68.1% at week 26; different populations and designs prevent a direct efficacy comparison or isolated C3GN estimate. The original VALIANT analysis did not show a significant histologic activity-score difference and did not formally test subsequent eGFR endpoints. Separately, the August 2026 US pegcetacoplan label includes reducing proteinuria and loss of kidney function in patients aged at least 12 with C3G or primary IC-MPGN; the inspected US iptacopan label covers proteinuria reduction in adults with C3G. Those regulatory statements do not establish lifelong prevention of kidney failure. Both labels warn of serious encapsulated-bacterial infections. This bounded, Consensus-assisted synthesis retains mixed-disease and assay limitations, incomplete screening and pending independent scientific review.
